contrastRules: Baseline body text is safe: --text on --bg computes 16.5:1 (light) and 16.1:1 (dark) - both AAA. Keep ALL long-form reading (dish stories, method, About manifesto) on this exact pairing. Hard floors everywhere: AA 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (>=24px, or >=18.66px/700).

--text-subtle (154 138 126) on the light --bg is only 3.12:1 and FAILS AA for body. Restrict it to large text, disabled states, and non-essential decoration in light mode. It reaches ~4.6:1 in dark mode (borderline) - still avoid it for dense metadata. Use --text-muted (6.1:1 light / 9.0:1 dark) for any caption/timestamp/ingredient metadata that must actually be read.

--primary (198 64 43) as colored text/link is 4.72:1 light and 5.26:1 dark - it passes AA but sits close to the floor. Never render primary-colored text at reduced opacity (no text-primary/70), below 16px in a thin weight, or over any surface other than --bg/--surface. The eyebrow (text-primary, all-caps 12px) is fine as-is.

--accent (orange 232 137 43) is only 2.44:1 on light paper - NEVER use it as text or as meaning-bearing icons on light surfaces. Reserve --accent for fills, large graphics, and text ONLY on charcoal/dark surfaces (where the lighter dark-mode accent reads bright).

CTA fills are safe: --primary-fg on --primary = 4.73:1 (light) / 5.23:1 (dark). Keep button labels >=14px semibold; do NOT tint the fill or drop label opacity - either breaches 4.5:1. Ghost buttons rely on their text for contrast (the --border ring is ~1.1:1 vs bg and is decorative), so keep ghost labels in --ink, never in --muted.

.text-gradient (primary->accent->persimmon) has a persimmon stop that measures ~1.9:1 on light paper - it fails even the 3:1 large-text bar. Use gradient text ONLY on dark surfaces and ONLY for large decorative display words; never for body copy and never on the light paper background.

Text-on-image scrims: never set text directly on raw photography. Require the COMPOSITED region under text to be <=0.18 relative luminance for white text (guarantees >=4.5:1). Default protection is a bottom-anchored linear-gradient from rgba(18,12,9,0) to rgba(18,12,9,0.92) over the lower ~45% where hero/card copy sits - a single flat 55-60% charcoal veil is NOT enough over bright, blown-out dishes.

Duotone (charcoal + accent) treatment helps but is not a guarantee - measure at the actual text pixels. Add a 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.6) text-shadow on any text over imagery as belt-and-suspenders, never as the primary legibility mechanism.

UI component & graphic contrast (WCAG 1.4.11 >=3:1): SpiceMeter fills, FlavorRadar strokes, ProgressRing tracks, Scoville gauge, chart series, active-filter chip states, form-field borders, and focus rings must all clear 3:1 against their adjacent background. Critically, the empty track vs the filled segment of any meter/gauge must ALSO differ by >=3:1 so the value is readable, not just pretty.

Never signal state by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): active filter chip, wouldCookAgain, spice level, batch status, and form errors each need a second cue - icon, weight, underline, fill, or label - so they survive color-blindness and low-contrast displays.

Re-validate every pairing in BOTH themes with a tool (axe DevTools / WebAIM formula) after the design fleet swaps the final palette onto these same CSS-variable tokens. The placeholder values are calibrated, but ANY palette change re-opens every ratio above.
motionRules: The global prefers-reduced-motion block already in index.css neutralizes CSS animation/transition/scroll-smooth - good. Extend it into JS: use Framer Motion's useReducedMotion() and branch every variant so reduced-motion users get the FINAL state instantly (opacity:1, no transform), not a 1ms-collapsed janky version.

No motion may gate comprehension. The hero headline, primary CTA, and nav must be in the DOM and legible at t=0. Reveals may fade/translate, but the 5-second-test content must read even if JS or motion never runs (progressive enhancement).

whileInView reveals: fade + 8-16px translate only, duration 300-500ms, ease cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), stagger 40-80ms per item, and viewport={{ once: true }} so content never re-animates on scroll-back. Cap simultaneous staggered children (~8) so a long mosaic doesn't ripple for seconds.

Hero Ken-Burns / slow scale: <=1.06 scale over 8-12s, transform + opacity only (GPU), NO autoplay video, parallax transform distance <25px to avoid vestibular triggers. Under reduced-motion the hero is a static image.

Auto-advancing content triggers WCAG 2.2.2: the Flavor Pulse marquee and any hero image rotation need a visible pause/stop control, >=5s per hero slide, and must never be the ONLY place trending info lives. The marquee pauses on hover, on focus-within, AND under reduced-motion.

Marquee/ticker technique: duplicate the track for the seamless loop with aria-hidden="true" on the duplicate, expose the real items once to the a11y tree, and provide a genuinely tabbable link list - not just scrolling text.

Magnetic CTA (60-100px cursor pull) is a pointer-only enhancement: disable it under reduced-motion, never let it move the button out from under the pointer, and never let it displace layout. Keyboard focus target stays put.
No scroll-hijacking and no forcing smooth-scroll against the user. ScrollProgress is decorative (aria-hidden) and must not be the only progress signal.
SkeletonShimmer / .animate-shimmer is motion too: under reduced-motion freeze it to a static neutral placeholder rather than a sweeping highlight.
Toasts and batch ready-alerts: entrance <=250ms, auto-dismiss >=6s (or persist with a close button). The text is the message - never rely on animation timing to convey it.

float-slow (7s) and spin-slow (34s) loops must stop under reduced-motion (already covered by the media query) and are reserved for ambient/decorative brand art only - never applied to anything a user must read or click.
readabilityRules: Measure: cap prose at the existing max-w-prose (68ch); ideal 60-70ch, hard ceiling 75ch. Method steps, tasting notes, and editorial intros all live in the 68ch column - never full-viewport-width paragraphs.

Body font-size floor is 16px (1rem); bump long-form editorial (dish story, About manifesto) to 17-18px. Metadata/captions/eyebrow may drop to 12-13px but ONLY in --text or --text-muted (never --text-subtle in light) and never for essential instructions.

Line-height: keep body at 1.6 (index.css default), raise dense editorial to 1.65-1.75. Headings stay tight - h1-h4 are 1.05 with -0.02em tracking (good); nudge multi-line H2/H3 to 1.1-1.15 so descenders don't collide. Keep text-wrap: pretty on p and balance on headings (already set).
Never justify text - ragged-right only; justification opens rivers in a 68ch column.
All-caps labels (eyebrow, category chips, nav) need positive tracking >=0.12em (eyebrow's 0.24em is right); never set all-caps below 11px and never all-caps a full running sentence.

Serif is DISPLAY-only: Fraunces on h1-h4, pull quotes, and oversized numbers; all UI, body, recipe steps, metadata, forms, and data stay in the sans (Inter). Do not set paragraphs or long method steps in the serif.

CRITICAL: Fraunces and Inter are referenced by name in the tokens but no @fontsource package is installed - they currently silently fall back to Georgia/system-ui. Install @fontsource-variable/fraunces + @fontsource-variable/inter, import them, and keep to 2 families total; the --font-accent var must alias Inter, not introduce a third family.

On data surfaces (Kitchen/Mise) resist the spreadsheet: stat tiles, cook-log rows, and passport stamps need >=16px padding and clear label/value hierarchy - label in --text-muted uppercase ~12px, value in Fraunces/display weight >=20px.
Interactive targets >=44x44px (exceed WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor): chips, RatingStars, FAB, filter toggles, and quick-look buttons all need a >=44px hit area even when the visual mark is smaller.
Cap the font program at 3-4 weights total (e.g. Inter 400/500/600 + Fraunces variable for display) to protect both hierarchy and the performance budget.
Enable tabular-nums (font-variant-numeric) on timers, Scoville/spice gauges, cook counts, and stats so digits don't jitter as values update.
semanticStructure: One <main> per route (Home/Explore/Dish/Kitchen/About), a single <header> housing GlobalNav, and a <footer> landmark. GlobalNav is <nav aria-label="Primary"> wrapping a <ul>.
Exactly one <h1> per page = the hero headline (Home POV statement, Dish title, "Explore", "Mise", About manifesto). No skipped heading levels: section titles are h2, sub-blocks h3.
Each major section is <section aria-labelledby="..."> tied to its SectionHeader id (Flavor Pulse, Featured Dish, Category grid, Kitchen boards, story rail).
A skip-to-content link is the first focusable element (visually hidden until focused) jumping to #main - essential given the tall cinematic hero above the content.

DishCard is an <article> made clickable by ONE link carrying the accessible name (the dish-title anchor with a stretched ::after), not nested interactive elements. Save/heart/quick-look are separate buttons with their own aria-labels, placed outside the card link to avoid nested interactives.

QuickLookModal is role="dialog" aria-modal="true" with aria-labelledby; trap focus, restore focus to the trigger on close, close on Escape and backdrop click, and mark the background inert/aria-hidden.

Data viz gets text equivalents: SpiceMeter/FlavorRadar/FlavorWheel/PassportMap are role="img" with a descriptive aria-label ("Heat 8 of 10, high umami, low sweetness"); decorative glyphs, grain overlay, GenerativeHeroArt, and the BrandMark flourish are aria-hidden="true" / role="presentation".

ProgressRing batch timers are role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax + aria-valuetext ("Kimchi - 3 days left, 60% complete"). StreakHeatmap is a <table> or labelled list with a text summary ("Cooked 4 of 7 days this week, 12-day streak"), never bare color squares.
Toasts/ready-alerts use an aria-live region: role="status"/polite for confirmations, role="alert"/assertive only for batch-ready and errors. ScrollProgress is aria-hidden.

Forms (NewsletterForm, TastingNoteForm): every input has an associated <label> (not placeholder-as-label); errors via aria-describedby + aria-invalid; RatingStars is a labelled radiogroup (fieldset/legend), not a loose row of icons; required state is stated in text, not color.

Controls: FilterChip is <button aria-pressed>; ThemeToggle is <button aria-pressed> with a text/aria label; FAB and all icon-only buttons carry aria-label; Breadcrumb is <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with aria-current="page" on the last crumb.

Keep <html lang="en"> (present), and make the theme toggle update color-scheme and the <meta name="theme-color"> in sync with its persisted, announced state (the pre-paint script in index.html already sets the initial class).
imagePerfBudget: Build SmartImage as mandatory infra: it renders the palette gradient (+ local SVG) fallback immediately behind the , wires onError to hide the broken while keeping the gradient, and reserves the box via CSS aspect-ratio (or width/height attrs) so there is ZERO layout shift whether the photo loads or fails.
Unsplash params on every URL: ?auto=format&fit=crop&w=<slot width>&q=<72-78>&dpr=<capped at 2>. auto=format serves AVIF/WebP; never request full-res originals; cap DPR at 2 (no 3x retina waste).
Responsive srcset + sizes on every non-hero image: widths ~[400,640,800,1200,1600] with a sizes attribute matching the grid columns, so phones fetch ~400-640px crops instead of 1600px.

Priority hero: exactly ONE LCP image per route loads eager - loading="eager" fetchpriority="high" plus a <link rel="preload" as="image" imagesrcset=...> for the hero crop. Every other image is loading="lazy" decoding="async".

Placeholders: the palette-derived gradient IS the required LQIP (guaranteed to render even offline). An optional tiny blurred Unsplash LQIP (w=24&blur=200) or inline base64 may layer on top, but the gradient must never be absent - no raw broken box, ever.
Weight budget: hero <=200KB (AVIF), grid card thumbnail <=60KB, initial above-the-fold image payload <=600KB, everything else lazy. QuickLook/modal images fetch only on open.

Core Web Vitals targets: LCP <2.5s (the hero is the LCP element - do not animate or defer it), CLS <0.1 (aspect-ratio boxes everywhere), INP <200ms (keep Framer Motion to transform/opacity so it never blocks the main thread).

content-visibility: auto on offscreen mosaic sections and long Kitchen boards so the browser skips their render work until near-viewport; pair with IntersectionObserver for infinite scroll and next-page prefetch.

Grain, duotone, category glyphs, and GenerativeHeroArt stay as CSS/inline-SVG (the committed local layer), never rasterized PNGs - this delivers the 'highly graphic' punch in KB, not MB, with zero network dependency.

Fonts are perf-critical: self-host via @fontsource, woff2 only, font-display: swap, subset to used unicode-range, preload the two critical faces (Fraunces display + Inter regular), cap at 3-4 weights. Fonts currently fall back to system - installing them fixes both brand fidelity and the FOUT/CLS swap.
Cap concurrent eager loads to the hero plus roughly the first visible row; add fetchpriority="low" to below-the-fold decorative imagery so it never contends with the LCP hero.
Test on a throttled Fast-3G / 4x-CPU profile AND with images.unsplash.com blocked, to prove the gradient/SVG fallback carries the 5-second impression when the CDN is unreachable.
focusStates: Never outline:none without a replacement. The base :focus-visible in index.css (2px solid --primary, 3px offset) is a good default - keep and extend it; do not strip it in component styles.

Use :focus-visible so mouse-click doesn't flash rings, but ensure EVERY interactive element receives it - links, buttons, chips, cards, RatingStars, FAB, ThemeToggle, gauges, and carousel controls. Any div-based custom control needs tabindex=0 + key handlers + the ring.

Focus-indicator contrast >=3:1 vs adjacent colors (WCAG 2.4.11/1.4.11). The --primary ring is 4.7:1 on paper and 3.7:1 on charcoal - fine on solid surfaces. Over photography/duotone cards it can wash out, so use a DUAL-tone ring there (2px --primary outline + a 2px bone box-shadow halo), or size the 3px offset so the ring lands on the solid page rather than the image.

Focus-not-obscured (WCAG 2.4.11 AA): the sticky translucent GlobalNav must not cover a focused element - add scroll-margin-top equal to the nav height on focusable targets so keyboard focus scrolls clear of the sticky bar.
Modal/QuickLook: trap focus within, move focus to the dialog on open, return it to the invoking control on close, and make the background inert.

Roving tabindex for composite widgets: the filter-chip group, EditorialRail/carousel, RatingStars, and FlavorWheel are single tab stops with arrow-key navigation, each item showing the ring as it is reached.

Magnetic/animated CTAs still show a stationary, fully-visible focus ring; the magnetic transform must not move the element away from where focus/pointer expects it, and focus styling is independent of hover.
Logical focus order matching visual/DOM order, skip-link first; verify by tabbing each page start-to-finish with no keyboard traps and no invisible focus.
Minimum focusable target 44x44px (exceeds WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor), and the visible focus ring must enclose the full hit area, not just an inner icon.
checklist: Automated audit: axe DevTools + Lighthouse a11y >=95 on all 5 routes, in BOTH light and dark, with zero critical violations.

Contrast sweep against the FINAL swapped palette (not just placeholders): confirm --text-subtle is not used for light-mode body, --accent is not used as light-mode text, and .text-gradient appears only on dark surfaces at display size.
Keyboard pass: tab each page top-to-bottom - skip link works, no traps, focus always visible (including over hero imagery), modals trap+restore, chips/RatingStars/carousel are arrow-navigable.

Screen-reader smoke test (VoiceOver + NVDA): landmarks announce, one h1/page, headings in order, images have alt or are hidden, meters/gauges/heatmap read their values, toasts announce, forms label correctly.

Reduced-motion pass: enable OS 'reduce motion' - hero scale, marquee, parallax, shimmer, and staggered reveals all quiet to static, content stays fully usable, and the 5-second impression still lands.
Content-at-t0 / no-JS: disable JS - hero headline, CTA, nav, and core copy still render and read (progressive enhancement holds).
Image resilience: block images.unsplash.com in devtools - every hero and card shows its gradient+SVG fallback, no broken boxes, CLS stays <0.1.
Performance budget on throttled mobile: LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, INP/TBT green; hero <=200KB, no image exceeds its slot size, fonts self-hosted with swap + preload (no system-font fallback flash).
Font & type QA: confirm @fontsource Fraunces/Inter actually load (not Georgia fallback), prose measures <=68ch, body >=16px, no justified text, tabular-nums on all data.
Alt-text content: every meaningful food image has descriptive alt (dish + treatment), decorative graphics are aria-hidden; no filename or bare 'image' alt.
Zoom/reflow: 200% browser zoom and a 320px-wide viewport - no horizontal scroll, no clipped text, sticky nav + filter FAB still usable (WCAG 1.4.10 / 1.4.4).
Color-independence: spice level, active filters, ratings, batch status, and errors are each distinguishable without color (icon/label/pattern).
Forms & errors: newsletter + tasting-note forms show labelled fields, inline errors tied via aria-describedby, success announced, RatingStars operable by keyboard.
Theme + meta: theme toggle persists, announces state, and updates color-scheme + theme-color meta; prefers-color-scheme honored on first paint (already scripted in index.html).
Target size & spacing: all controls >=44px hit area with adequate spacing; mobile filter FAB and back-to-top are reachable and non-overlapping.
Real-device check (iOS Safari + Android Chrome): backdrop-blur/glass legibility, sticky-nav focus obscuring, and marquee/hero pause controls all behave.
